result:
Both commits exist, and I did not merge.

- **Ancestor:** No. `git merge-base --is-ancestor side HEAD` says `side` is not an ancestor of `feat/2.1.327-next`. The two branches have diverged from the same base.
- **Conflict:** Yes. `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD side` exited 1 with `CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in plans/rebuild/README.md`. Both branches changed line 1 of that file, and it is the only conflicted file.

The commits:
- `side` has `581517d1a`, which sets line 1 to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (side)`.
- `feat/2.1.327-next` has `640ff9022`, which sets line 1 to `# claudetto Rebuild Plan (main line)`.

I'm back on `feat/2.1.327-next` and the working tree is clean. `merge-tree` only computes the merge in memory, so no branch or file was changed by the check.
